Exoskeletons grown with this Charm have one point of bashing and lethal soak for every mote spent in their creation, as well as a mobility penalty equal to half their soak rating (rounded down). Characters cannot spend more motes building an Ivory Blossom Carapace than their Stamina + Resistance, no matter how many times they use this Charm in a scene to add additional plating. Characters wearing armor cannot use this Charm.
cost: 1 mote per 1B/1L, plus one lethal health level
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Resistance tree ('Resistance 1'), p. 182 (PDF 183); effect text continues onto the following page. The 'plus one lethal health level' cost component and its exact interaction with the per-mote soak cost was cut off at the bottom of this render; flagged for re-verification against a cleaner render before promotion.

name: Bone Arsenal Method
summary: This multipurpose Charm allows characters to extrude spikes and razor spines over their entire body, or to grow weapons directly from their limbs, at the cost of an unusually high mote outlay.
requirements: Minimum Brawl 2; Minimum Resistance 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Ivory Blossom Carapace.
mechanics: This multipurpose Charm allows characters to extrude spikes and razor spines over their entire body, or to grow weapons from their limbs. If used to grow spines, the Charm costs 8 motes, 1 Willpower and one lethal health level. The lattice of blades provides an additional soak of 2B/2L that stacks with soak bonuses from other Charms. Additionally, characters encased in blades can inflict lethal damage with all 'unarmed' hand-to-hand attacks, including wrestling maneuvers such as clinches and tackles. Finally, anyone who grapples a character with spines or strikes her barehanded must immediately soak a number of dice of lethal damage equal to his own Strength. Growing melee weapons with Bone Arsenal Method costs one lethal health level, as well as 1 mote for every +1 invested in Speed, Accuracy, Defense or lethal damage (all of which begin at a rating of 0). Characters cannot raise any of these Traits higher than their permanent Essence. Although weapons created with this Charm can take virtually any form, they remain obvious extensions of their creator's skeleton and cannot be dropped or taken away unless severed. Characters with Ivory Blossom Carapace activated do not have to spend fresh health levels to use any aspect of this Charm, though other costs remain unchanged. All protrusions and weapons created by Bone Arsenal Method retract into their owner's skeleton when the Charm expires.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Resistance tree ('Resistance 1'), p. 182 (PDF 183). Unusual in requiring a minimum rating in a second Ability (Brawl 2) alongside Resistance.

name: Crimson Petal Armor
summary: Blood gushes from every pore of the character's skin and shapes itself into a suit of enchanted armor for the scene, flowing back into the body through the mouth when the Charm expires.
requirements: Minimum Resistance 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Ivory Blossom Carapace.
mechanics: Upon activation of this Charm, blood gushes from every pore of the character's skin and shapes itself into a suit of enchanted armor. This liquid armor flows and shifts with its wearer's every motion, yet hardens to turn aside blows as if it were made of the finest steel. When this Charm expires, the glistening armor flows back into its creator's body through his mouth. Apart from its appearance, Crimson Petal Armor follows the same rules as Ivory Blossom Carapace, except that its liquid armor is virtually weightless and has no mobility penalty. Characters cannot activate this Charm while using Ivory Blossom Carapace (or vice versa), just as with any other armor. Characters only need to spend Willpower the first time they activate this Charm during a scene.
cost: 1 mote per 1B/1L, 1 Willpower, one lethal health level
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Resistance tree ('Resistance 1'), p. 182 (PDF 183). The one-time cost of the health level/Willpower 'only applies the first time it is used during a given scene' per the top-of-page continuation text on p. 183 (PDF 184).

name: Flowing Wound Defense
summary: Capstone of the first Midnight Caste Resistance tree; building on Crimson Petal Armor's principle, the Abyssal can momentarily liquefy her body and possessions to shrug off a blow or assault entirely, a form of perfect defense.
requirements: Minimum Resistance 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Crimson Petal Armor.
mechanics: Building on the principle of Crimson Petal Armor, this Charm allows an Abyssal to momentarily liquefy her body and possessions to shrug off any blow or assault. Upon impact, she seamlessly melts into gore and then re-solidifies, allowing the attack to pass harmlessly through her without resistance. This process is particularly gruesome when defending against falls and other full-body trauma, as the character splatters into a mass of congealed blood and immediately reforms without injury. Characters using this Charm can take no damage from a single attack but must contend with secondary effects normally. This invulnerability duplicates the protection granted by the Solar Charm Adamant Skin Technique and is a form of perfect defense. A character must invoke Flowing Wound Defense after his opponent spends any motes to activate Charms but before the foe makes her actual attack roll.
cost: 5 motes, 1 Willpower, one lethal health level
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Resistance tree ('Resistance 1'), p. 183 (PDF 184). Cross-references core Exalted p. 177 for the Solar Adamant Skin Technique comparison. Closes out the first Resistance tree (8 Charms: Spirit-Hardened Frame, Ivory Blossom Carapace, Bone Arsenal Method, Crimson Petal Armor, Flowing Wound Defense, Snake Bites Its Tail, Scarlet Venom Technique, Plague Knows Its Master).

name: Plague Knows Its Master
summary: Some Abyssal Exalted become highly resistant to disease as a result of their consecration to the Malfeans, subtracting from the difficulty of resisting infection and disease until the roll is automatically won or lost.
requirements: Minimum Resistance 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Spirit-Hardened Frame.
mechanics: Some Abyssal Exalted become highly resistant to disease as a result of their consecration to the Malfeans. As with Ox-Body Technique, this Charm can be purchased more times than as if it were a Charm. Players of characters with Plague Knows Its Master subtract their characters' permanent Essence from the difficulty of all Stamina + Resistance and Stamina + Endurance rolls to resist or throw off infection and disease. In the case of avoiding infected wounds, this reduction is cumulative with the -2 modifier all Exalted share. If the final difficulty of a modified roll is reduced below 1, the character automatically avoids contracting the illness or successfully purges it from his system (as appropriate to the roll in question).
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Resistance tree ('Resistance 1'), p. 183 (PDF 184). Flagged for re-verification: 'this Charm can be purchased more times than as if it were a Charm' reads as a garbled transcription of a comparison to Ox-Body Technique's repeatable-purchase rule; re-check exact wording against a cleaner render before promotion.

name: Snake Bites Its Tail
summary: The character amplifies her metabolism with Essence, strengthening her body's resistance to poison for the rest of the scene, with stronger poisons requiring an active resistance roll.
requirements: Minimum Resistance 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Spirit-Hardened Frame.
mechanics: The character amplifies her metabolism with Essence, strengthening her body's resistance to poison. For the rest of the scene, the Exalt nullifies any poison she is exposed to that has a resistance difficulty lower than her permanent Essence. Against stronger poisons, the Exalt's player may add her character's Essence in automatic successes to her Stamina + Resistance roll. Characters need not evoke this Charm before exposure to toxins, so long as they activate it before rolling to resist. Incidental toxins such as spoiled food are generally considered difficulty 1 or 2 for the purposes of this Charm. Characters protected by this Charm may safely consume an additional dose of alcoholic drinks equal to their Resistance without penalty.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Resistance tree ('Resistance 1'), p. 184 (PDF 185).

name: Scarlet Venom Technique
summary: Corrupted in body and spirit by the power of the Malfeans, the Abyssal's blood permanently becomes tainted with vile poison equivalent to arrow frog venom, an effect that cannot be turned off.
requirements: Minimum Resistance 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Snake Bites Its Tail.
mechanics: Corrupted in body and spirit by the power of the Malfeans, some Abyssal Exalted find their very blood tainted with vile poison. Once a character purchases this Charm, venom suffuses every fluid in her body. This poison has the same statistics as arrow frog venom. Players of living beings consuming or otherwise internalizing these tainted fluids (such as through kissing or more intimate contact) must succeed at a Stamina + Resistance roll or have their characters suffer the full deleterious effects of the poison. This Charm cannot be turned off or suppressed -- the corruption is irreversible.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Resistance tree ('Resistance 1'), p. 184 (PDF 185). Cross-references core Exalted p. 243 for arrow frog venom's statistics.

name: Armor-Calling Kata
summary: Root of the second Midnight Caste Resistance tree; with this Charm, an Abyssal can dramatically speed the process of donning her armor, summoning it from Elsewhere via a liquid shroud of darkness.
requirements: Minimum Resistance 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can dramatically speed the process of donning his armor. He need only gesture to it, and his anima flows out to enfold the armor in a liquid shroud of darkness. By the end of the turn, the anima slithers back and fastens the armor perfectly in place. The character must have the armor readily available and at hand to use this Charm no further away than his Essence in yards.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Resistance tree ('Resistance 2'), p. 184 (PDF 185).

name: Void-Banished Mail
summary: An Abyssal who knows this Charm can store his armor Elsewhere, recalling it only as needed for battle by concentrating and summoning it back onto his person with a scream of torn air.
requirements: Minimum Resistance 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Armor-Calling Kata.
mechanics: An Abyssal who knows this Charm can store his armor Elsewhere, recalling it only as needed for battle. The character must be wearing his armor with all its straps and fastenings fitted properly to banish it. If these conditions are met, the armor vanishes in a flash of ghostly light. At any time, the character may concentrate and summon his armor to reappear on his person, causing it to reappear with a scream of torn air. A character can only have one suit of armor stored Elsewhere at a time and may not recall it unless she is unarmored to receive it. Void-Banished Mail cannot banish armor substantially larger than the Exalt, so it is impossible to hide warstriders with this Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Resistance tree ('Resistance 2'), p. 184 (PDF 185).

name: Inauspicious Shadow Plate
summary: Capstone of the second Midnight Caste Resistance tree; the Abyssal's anima hardens, encasing her in a suit of obsidian-black plate mail that is an expression of her own personality and temperament.
requirements: Minimum Resistance 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Void-Banished Mail.
mechanics: The Abyssal's anima hardens, encasing her in a suit of obsidian-black plate mail. This armor is an expression of the character's soul, and thus, it reflects her personality and temperament. It may be ornate and decorated with weeping faces and skulls or elegant in its simplicity -- it is the character's ideal armor. Inauspicious Shadow Plate provides 10L/10B soak, with only a -1 mobility penalty. For an additional 2 motes, the deathknight can also grow a sweeping black cape that moves and flows of its own accord to entangle and snag incoming blows. This cloak acts like a shield, increasing the difficulty of all attacks against the Exalt by +1.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Resistance tree ('Resistance 2'), p. 185 (PDF 186). Closes out the Midnight Caste Resistance section (11 Charms total across two sub-trees).

name: Essence Engorgement Technique
summary: Root of the Midnight Caste Survival tree; lacking ready sources of Essence apart from cannibalism, Abyssal Exalted with this repeatable Charm offset that weakness by bloating their animas with stolen power.
requirements: Minimum Survival 1; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Lacking ready sources of Essence apart from cannibalism, Abyssal Exalted must often conserve their power in Creation. Deathknights with this Charm can offset this weakness somewhat by bloating their animas with stolen power. For each time this Charm is taken, the Abyssal adds an additional 10 motes to his Peripheral Essence pool. However, the Exalt can only fill this extra capacity by consuming flesh or blood or by using Essence-draining magic. The character cannot recharge this bonus capacity with Hearthstones, respiration or any other passive means. Characters cannot take this Charm more times than their permanent Essence score.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Survival tree ('Survival 1'), p. 185 (PDF 186).

name: Blood-Feasting Technique
summary: Once an Abyssal masters this Charm, he can subsist entirely on a diet of human blood, drinking enough per day to replace his body's need for regular food while forgoing solid nutrition entirely.
requirements: Minimum Survival 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Essence Engorgement Technique.
mechanics: Once an Abyssal masters this Charm, he can subsist entirely on a diet of human blood. The character must drink a number of health levels per day equal to his permanent Essence if he wishes to replace his body's need for regular food. While subsisting on blood, characters suffer no dietary deficiencies. Many deathknights who learn this Charm find their palettes prefer the sweet taste of life to blander solid food. Note that blood consumed specifically as sustenance for this Charm does not provide Essence.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Survival tree ('Survival 1'), p. 185 (PDF 186).

name: Superior Predator Style
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal can intensify his aura of menace to ward off animals, terrifying herbivores and domesticated beasts into flight while giving even magical predators pause.
requirements: Minimum Survival 1; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can intensify his aura of menace to ward off animals. Herbivores and domesticated beasts avoid the character completely and panic if directly confronted. Most non-magical predators keep their distance, fighting only as a last resort if cornered. This Charm has less effect on magical beasts and super-predators such as tyrant lizards and siaka. Such beings can overcome the aversion with a successful Willpower roll, although they still suffer a +1 difficulty to attack the Exalt.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Survival tree, p. 185 (PDF 186). This Charm's own header lists 'Prerequisite Charms: None' and it is not shown in the small 'Survival 1' tree diagram on this page (which shows only Essence Engorgement Technique -> Blood-Feasting Technique); likely the first Charm of a separate 'Survival 2' tree whose diagram was not visible on this render. Flagged for re-verification of its tree placement against a later page render.

name: Enduring Huntsman Method
summary: Root of the 'Survival 3' sub-tree; a deathknight with this Charm gains unnatural resilience to hostile environments regardless of attire or preparation.
requirements: Minimum Survival 3; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: With this Charm, a character gains unnatural resilience to hostile environments, regardless of attire or preparation. She can withstand brutal extremes of temperature without ill effect and need never fear hypothermia, frostbite, parasites, sand blindness or any other hazard of the wilderness. This resistance applies to virtually any condition a human body could actually survive, however briefly. Thus, a character could trudge naked through a blizzard without discomfort but would not have an easier time breathing underwater or surviving a raging bonfire. Ultimately, the limits of this Charm are left to Storyteller discretion.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Survival tree ('Survival 3'), p. 186 (PDF 187). Root of a four-branch sub-tree (Maze-Unraveling Concentration, Infallible Barghest Mien, Sheltering Interment Prana, Underworld Foraging Technique).

name: Sheltering Interment Prana
summary: An Abyssal can mystically sink into the earth and bury herself alive, entering suspended animation while interred.
requirements: Minimum Survival 3; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Enduring Huntsman Method.
mechanics: Pulling his arms and legs together like a corpse ready for burial, an Abyssal with this Charm can mystically sink into the earth underground, leaving no trace of excavation on the surface. The character slips into a state of suspended animation for the duration and does not breathe, although he still hungers normally. Sheltering Interment Prana lasts one hour for every 3 motes spent, unless the torpid character is injured or uncovered by digging. Once the Charm ends for whatever reason, the character arises to the surface in a shower of dirt and immediately regains consciousness. Characters may regain Essence while interred (assuming they are in a location that permits it), although motes used to power the Charm remain committed during its duration.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Survival tree ('Survival 3'), p. 186 (PDF 187).

name: Underworld Foraging Technique
summary: By definition, few environments are as inhospitable and lifeless as the dim recesses of the Underworld; this Charm allows an Abyssal to readily consume spectral food and derive full nourishment from her meal.
requirements: Minimum Survival 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Enduring Huntsman Method.
mechanics: The food of ghosts and the strange beasts that lurk in the realm of the dead afford little in the way of palatable meat. With this Charm, however, an Abyssal may readily consume spectral food and derive full nourishment from her meal.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Survival tree ('Survival 3'), pp. 186-187 (PDF 187-188).

name: Maze-Unraveling Concentration
summary: An Abyssal can mentally unlock the twisting paths of a labyrinth to find a desired course or egress, adding automatic successes to a simple task to navigate a maze or similarly convoluted network of passages.
requirements: Minimum Survival 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Enduring Huntsman Method.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can mentally unlock the twisting paths of a labyrinth to find a desired course or egress. The character can add a permanent Essence rating in automatic successes to a simple task to navigate a maze or similarly convoluted network of passages. This Charm aids in navigating the Labyrinth beneath the Underworld to a lesser degree. The Ebon Maze defies sane comprehension, both for its size and alien geometry. Characters can only unravel short stretches at a time, and this Charm only applies to a single navigation roll.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Survival tree ('Survival 3'), p. 187 (PDF 188).

name: Infallible Barghest Mien
summary: An Abyssal can pursue a quarry with supernatural prowess and determination, adding a die per mote to a single tracking roll and never losing the trail regardless of environment.
requirements: Minimum Survival 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Enduring Huntsman Method.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can pursue a quarry with supernatural prowess and determination. The player can add one die per mote to a single tracking roll to track a single target individual. This target must be decided when the Charm is invoked and cannot later be changed. Bonus dice granted from this Charm apply to all tracking attempts until the character finds his quarry or gives up his hunt, although this Charm cannot more than double a character's dice pool. Infallible Barghest Mien aids in tracking regardless of environment; the character can stalk his quarry through the twisting streets of a necropolis as readily as any wilderness. Characters may only benefit from one application of this Charm at a time. Characters using this Charm are considered supernatural trackers.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Survival tree ('Survival 3'), p. 187 (PDF 188).

name: Ghost Leaves No Trail
summary: Capstone of the Midnight Caste Survival tree; for its duration the character passes unobtrusively as a phantom, leaving no footprints, scent or any sign of her passing detectable by conventional means.
requirements: Minimum Survival 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Infallible Barghest Mien.
mechanics: For the duration of this Charm, the character passes unobtrusively as a phantom. She leaves no footprints or scent or any sign of her passing that can be detected by conventional means. The character can also extend this protection to a maximum number of companions equal to her permanent Essence rating at a cost of 5 motes each. Only characters with supernatural tracking abilities can hope to follow an Exalt shrouded by this Charm, and such attempts are resolved through a normal tracking contest.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Midnight Caste Survival tree ('Survival 3'), p. 187 (PDF 188). Closes out the Midnight Caste Survival section (11 Charms total) and, with it, all five Midnight Caste Charm trees (Endurance, Performance, Presence, Resistance, Survival).

name: Fault-Finding Scrutiny
summary: Root of the Daybreak Caste Craft tree; by attuning her gaze to the seeds of entropy in all things, an Abyssal using this Charm can perceive the weak points of any inanimate object.
requirements: Minimum Craft 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: By attuning her gaze to the seeds of entropy in all things, an Abyssal using this Charm can perceive the weak points of any inanimate object. Fracture lines and hidden cracks appear stained oily black, while even the slightest traces of rot or rust glow hideous shades of brown and red. With this knowledge, characters may exploit or repair the flaws they find with greater facility. Characters attempting to repair objects identified with this Charm may double any Craft-related dice pool to do so. However, such repairs require the same effort, time and tools as normal. Similarly, characters attacking a scrutinized object's weak points count extra successes twice for the purpose of determining damage with their first strike. Subsequent attacks do not receive this bonus unless the character uses Fault-Finding Scrutiny to reevaluate the object's weaknesses.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Craft tree, p. 187 (PDF 188). Root of Daybreak Caste, which trades Chapter Five's melee/social Caste Abilities for Craft, Investigation, Lore, Medicine and Occult.

name: (Material) Withering Method
summary: Actually three separate Charms (Wood-, Metal- and Stone-Withering Method) that the Exalt channels as corrosive Essence directly into an object, triggering rapid decay that disintegrates it to nothing within seconds.
requirements: Minimum Craft 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Fault-Finding Scrutiny.
mechanics: The Exalt channels corrosive Essence directly into an object, triggering rapid decay. (Material) Withering Method is actually three separate Charms, each encompassing a different substance: wood, metal and stone. Although the three versions decay their respective material differently -- rotting, rusting or crumbling as appropriate -- the final result is the same: the object disintegrates to nothing within seconds. This Charm can only be used on objects the size of a large weapon or a single suit of armor. (Material) Withering Method has no effect on enchanted items, including those made from or reinforced by the Five Magical Materials. All versions of this Charm have a range of (the Abyssal's permanent Essence x 10) yards and may only be used once per turn.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Craft tree, pp. 187-188 (PDF 188-189). Modeled here as a single row for the shared mechanic; the book treats Wood-, Metal- and Stone-Withering Method as three discrete purchasable Charms, and Form-Restoring Touch requires all three to be known before it can be learned.

name: Decay Resistance Preparation
summary: This Charm makes an object highly resistant to natural and unnatural forms of decay, including corrosion, rust, rot and even simple weathering.
requirements: Minimum Craft 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Fault-Finding Scrutiny.
mechanics: This Charm makes an object highly resistant to natural and unnatural forms of decay, including corrosion, rust, rot and even simple weathering. For ordinary wear and tear, treated objects endure at least 10 times as long as untreated counterparts. Against more aggressive causes of decay, such as acid baths or bolts of raw entropy, objects have double the usual soak or resistance dice pool. Although this enhancement is permanent, it only protects against decay. Treated objects have no additional resilience against other sources of damage and may be cut, burnt or otherwise broken as normal. This Charm does not work on living beings.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Craft tree, p. 188 (PDF 189).

name: Bone Graft Technique
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal can fashion prosthetics of iron and carved bone and affix them to living flesh as replacements for missing limbs, with the resulting limb owing its sturdy construction a +2L/2B soak bonus.
requirements: Minimum Craft 4; Minimum Medicine 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Decay Resistance Preparation, Flesh-Mending Discipline.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can fashion prosthetics of iron and carved bone and affix them to living flesh as replacements for missing limbs. The Exalt must first build the actual prosthesis, which requires a number of creation rolls as outlined on pp. 245-246 of Exalted, usually using Craft (Necrosurgery). If successful, the character can use this Charm to join the implant with its host. The recipient must commit Essence (or Willpower, in the case of mortals) to attune the device to her life force. Generally, a hand requires 3 motes or 1 point of Willpower, while a full arm requires 5 motes or 2 Willpower. Entire legs are as many as 8 motes or 3 Willpower. So long as the costs remain attuned, the prosthetics behave entirely as their organic counterpart. Owing to their sturdy construction, prosthetics designed with this Charm have a +2L/2B soak against damage of any sort.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Simple. Note: this Charm's own prerequisite entry cross-references Flesh-Mending Discipline, a Medicine 1 Charm (see flesh-mending-discipline row), showing the Craft and Medicine trees interlock for Daybreak Caste.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Craft tree, p. 188 (PDF 189).

name: Form-Restoring Touch
summary: Capstone of the Daybreak Caste Craft tree; this Charm allows a character to repair any broken object, so long as some fragment remains, painstakingly binding shards with wisps of memory dredged from the winds of the Underworld.
requirements: Minimum Craft 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: All three (Material) Withering Method Charms, Decay Resistance Preparation.
mechanics: This Charm allows a character to repair any broken object, so long as some fragment remains. She must spend a number of hours working on the object (10 minus her permanent Essence), while she painstakingly joins shards and binds them with wisps of memory dredged from the winds of the Underworld. This Charm cannot remake intangible items (such as broken promises) or restore objects more yards in radius than the character's permanent Essence. Form-Restoring Touch can repair items of First Age manufacture but can do nothing to mend those whose magic has fled or been exhausted.
cost: 10 motes, 1 Willpower, one lethal health level
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Craft tree, p. 188 (PDF 189). Closes out the Daybreak Caste Craft section (5 Charms total, treating (Material) Withering Method as one row).

name: Excellent Inquisitor Attitude
summary: Root of the Daybreak Caste Investigation tree; the character grows cold and detached, studying the world with heartless scrutiny, adding bonus dice to an extended Investigation task for every mote of Essence spent.
requirements: Minimum Investigation 1; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The character grows cold and detached, studying the world with heartless scrutiny. For each mote of Essence spent, the player may add 1 die to an Investigation roll, though the number of bonus dice can add no more than double the character's base Attribute + Ability pool. This bonus may be maintained for extended investigations, research or interrogation sessions. However, the bonus only applies to a single specific task that can last no longer than a scene. This Charm can only enhance one task at a time. For Example: Prince of Shadows has a prisoner brought before him. He uses Excellent Inquisitor Attitude for the purpose of interrogating her, spending 4 motes to gain four bonus dice. Since he plans to spend the full scene torturing his captive, this bonus applies to all related actions in the scene, such as his effort to search the prisoner's belongings or to notice clues evident in her dress or accent, since these tasks are unrelated to the interrogation.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Investigation tree, p. 189 (PDF 190).

name: Deception-Piercing Stare
summary: This Charm allows a character to look at an individual and perceive the slight taint of unrighteousness left by deliberate lies; infallible within its limits but only detects deliberate falsehoods.
requirements: Minimum Investigation 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: Excellent Inquisitor Attitude.
mechanics: This Charm allows a character to look at an individual and perceive the slight taint of unrighteousness left by deliberate lies. This Charm is infallible within its limits, but only detects deliberate falsehoods. Characters who sincerely believe a falsehood do not register as having lied, nor do characters who answer in an unclear manner or withhold information (including those who refuse to answer at all). Deception-Piercing Stare cannot compel or discern truth.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Investigation tree, p. 189 (PDF 190).

name: Unsurpassed Interrogation Method
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal inflicts terrible pain on anyone who disrespectfully answers her questions with lies or silence, forcing a Willpower-vs-Essence contest with painful backlash on failure.
requirements: Minimum Investigation 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Deception-Piercing Stare.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal inflicts terrible pain on anyone who disrespectfully answers her questions with lies or silence. This Charm applies only to the extended interrogation of one individual whose Willpower + Essence is less than the Exalt's Manipulation + Investigation. The player of an affected character must reflexively roll Willpower against a difficulty of the Exalt's permanent Essence whenever he attempts to lie or withhold relevant information. If the roll succeeds, the character can answer or remain silent as he wishes, although the Exalt can repeat the question on the following turn if she is dissatisfied with the response. If the roll fails, the victim suffers one unsoakable level of bashing damage and spends the rest of the turn in agony. The Abyssal may not control or lessen this damage after invoking Unsurpassed Interrogation Method except by prematurely ending the Charm. It is possible for victims to kill themselves with repeated lies, although they are not punished for speaking falsehoods they sincerely believe. The Abyssal can normally ask only one question per turn, though complicated matters may require additional turns to phrase an answer. This Charm can only be used on a given target once per week.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Investigation tree, pp. 189-190 (PDF 190-191).

name: Incomparable Agony Technique
summary: Building on Unsurpassed Interrogation Method, this Charm allows a character to torture victims with the force of her preternatural will, inflicting resisted bashing or lethal damage or draining Willpower from the victim's pool.
requirements: Minimum Investigation 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Unsurpassed Interrogation Method.
mechanics: Building on the principle of Unsurpassed Interrogation Method, this Charm allows a character to torture victims with the force of her preternatural will. The Exalt's player must make a Conviction + Essence roll, resisted by the victim's Willpower + Essence. For every success rolled beyond the victim's, the Abyssal can psychically inflict one level of unsoakable bashing or lethal damage or remove one point of temporary Willpower from the victim's pool. If so desired, the Abyssal's player can apply successes less severe than actually rolled. Characters reduced below zero temporary Willpower with this Charm gain a derangement chosen by the Storyteller and fall catatonic for the remainder of the scene. Wounds inflicted by this Charm take whatever form the Abyssal desires, although stigmata and artistically broken bones are common motifs. The Charm only affects a single restrained or willingly motionless victim within 5 yards of the Exalt, severely limiting its combat application. Additionally, the Charm has no effect on characters with a higher permanent Essence than the Abyssal.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Investigation tree, p. 190 (PDF 191).

name: Cunning Scrutiny Style
summary: Through careful examination of undisturbed physical evidence at a scene, the character can mentally reconstruct the process that led to that evidence, such as the angle of attack or type of weapon used on a body.
requirements: Minimum Investigation 3; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: Excellent Inquisitor Attitude.
mechanics: Through careful examination of undisturbed physical evidence at a scene, the character can mentally reconstruct the process that led to that evidence. For example, characters finding a dead body may analyze its wounds to determine the angle of attack, the type of weapon used, etc. Although primarily employed for forensic purposes, this Charm may just as easily reconstruct the evidence left by liaisons or the details of an abandoned campsite. This Charm functions automatically only so long as there is abundant physical evidence. Where evidence is lacking -- or has been disturbed -- the player must instead roll Perception + Investigation at a difficulty determined by the amount of tampering. Success allows the character to reconstruct events normally.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Investigation tree, p. 190 (PDF 191).

name: Corpse Questioning Technique
summary: Potent memories linger in the flesh, even after death; this Charm allows an Abyssal to extract those memories, partially animating a corpse or disembodied head to answer her questions.
requirements: Minimum Investigation 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Unsurpassed Interrogation Method, Cunning Scrutiny Style.
mechanics: Potent memories linger in the flesh, even after death. This Charm allows an Abyssal to extract those memories, partially animating a corpse or disembodied head to answer her questions. Cadavers ensorcelled by this Charm open their mouths and speak in whispering monotones but have no personality of their own. Although corpses cannot lie, either directly or by significant omission, their memories rot along with their flesh. For every full week a body has been dead, its Intelligence is reduced by one dot, to a minimum rating of 1. Corpses can only understand and answer languages known in life and remain silent if asked questions they do not understand. Unearthed skulls can barely whisper 'yes' or 'no' to the simplest queries, while freshly slain cadavers may answer virtually any question put to them. Magic that forestalls physical decay of a corpse also preserves the Intelligence of a corpse.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Investigation tree, p. 191 (PDF 192).

name: Lingering Echo Meditation
summary: Capstone of the Daybreak Caste Investigation tree; important or emotionally charged events leave a psychic imprint that this Charm can induce as a vivid flashback of the events leading to the imprint.
requirements: Minimum Investigation 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Corpse Questioning Technique.
mechanics: Important or emotionally charged events leave a psychic imprint on the location or objects involved. Such imprints can last for years or even centuries, depending on their potency. By touching a marked place or object and attuning his mind to its passion, an Abyssal with this Charm can induce a vivid flashback of the events leading to the imprint. If the scrutinized object has multiple associations, the strongest passion usually prevails -- but not always. Visions triggered by this Charm affect all senses -- in effect, the character is mentally transported to the time and place of the imprinted passion. Though flashbacks only last a few seconds in reality, they can appear to take minutes or even hours depending on the depth and intensity. Visions are always colored by their dominant passion. A violent murder scene may have a slight red tint or a frenetic jerkiness. Similarly, a couple shown at their wedding might appear softer and more beautiful -- almost ethereal. In no case can a character take any action in a vision or even choose her vantage point. As an optional rule, a Storyteller can trigger this Charm reflexively whenever a character touches an object sufficiently charged with emotional energy. In such cases, the Essence cost remains the same, but the Willpower requirement is waived since the resulting vision is not an act of will. Such flashbacks should enhance mood and move a plot forward. They should never be used frivolously or as an excuse to drain a character's Willpower.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Investigation tree, pp. 191-192 (PDF 192-193). Closes out the Daybreak Caste Investigation section (7 Charms total).

name: Crypt Bolt
summary: Root of the Daybreak Caste Lore tree; the character reaches out her hand and a bolt of crackling darkness leaps from her outstretched palm, inflicting damage that manifests as sudden decay.
requirements: Minimum Lore 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The character reaches out her hand, and a bolt of crackling darkness leaps from his outstretched palm. Damage inflicted by this Charm manifests as sudden decay: metal corrodes and rusts, while wood and flesh wither away as though blighted by disease and aging. The player rolls Dexterity + Athletics or Thrown (whichever he prefers) to hit, applying an Accuracy bonus equal to his permanent Essence. This attack has a range of (the character's permanent Essence x 10) yards and does a base damage of 2L for each mote of Essence spent.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Lore tree, p. 191 (PDF 192).

name: Essence-Scattering Blast
summary: The character extends her arm and a bolt of coruscating energy flies from her fingertips; strikes against a being with an Essence pool envelop them in ribbons of black lightning that drains their energy.
requirements: Minimum Lore 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Crypt Bolt.
mechanics: The character extends her arm, and a bolt of coruscating energy flies from her fingertips. If this bolt strikes a being with an Essence pool, it envelops her in ribbons of black lightning and drains her energy. Although it inflicts no damage, Essence-Scattering Blast otherwise follows the same rules as Crypt Bolt with regards to its Range, Accuracy and roll to hit. Victims struck by this attack lose 1 mote of Essence for every mote spent activating this Charm, plus a number of additional motes equal to the Exalt's permanent Essence. If applicable, victims lose Peripheral Essence before Personal Essence. This attack dissipates harmlessly if it hits anything besides a magical being, including unExalted mortals. A character cannot spend more motes on this Charm than his Stamina + Lore.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Lore tree, p. 191 (PDF 192).

name: Breath-Draining Prana
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal may feed on a target's life force directly even without touching her, soaking the drained lethal damage with Stamina and regaining Essence in the process.
requirements: Minimum Lore 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Essence-Scattering Blast.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal may feed on a target's life force directly even without touching her. The player rolls Willpower. Each success rolls one die of lethal damage. For every level of damage actually inflicted, the Abyssal regains 1 mote of Essence. This Charm can also target the Essence pool of a magical being, with successes draining Essence motes directly on a one-for-one basis. So long as the Exalt drains fewer motes than a target's Stamina, she may not even notice the loss -- attributing the sudden weakness to some other cause. However, Essence drained from another magical being's pool glimmers in the air as it flows out of the victim's mouth and into the deathknight's own. This Charm can target any being in the deathknight's line of sight.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Lore tree, p. 192 (PDF 193).

name: Radiant Blight Technique
summary: By forcing death Essence into the land around her, the deathknight can destroy all the plant life in the vicinity and seriously damage the creatures that live there.
requirements: Minimum Lore 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Crypt Bolt.
mechanics: By forcing death Essence into the land around her, the deathknight can destroy all the plant life in the vicinity and seriously damage the creatures that live there. The Abyssal's player rolls Charisma + Lore. All plants within a circular area equal to the number of successes rolled in yards wither and die. All animals and people within that radius, including other Exalted, suffer dice of lethal damage equal to the character's permanent Essence. The damage from this Charm is soaked only with the character's natural soak.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Lore tree, p. 192 (PDF 193).

name: Wyld Shield Meditation
summary: Whereas the Wyld embodies growth and untamed possibility and the Underworld represents death and ultimate stagnation, an Abyssal with this Charm can channel her death-tainted Essence to shield her and her possessions from the Wyld's warping effects.
requirements: Minimum Lore 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Crypt Bolt.
mechanics: Whereas the Wyld embodies growth and untamed possibility, the Underworld represents death and ultimate stagnation. As such, Abyssal Exalted with this Charm can channel their death-tainted Essence to shield them from the warping effects of Wyld energies. With this Charm invoked, the character and her possessions (an amount that can equal a fully laden horse if mounted) can venture in the most chaotic regions of the Wyld without suffering any change of form. Additionally, the character can add her permanent Essence to her soak (and applicable rolls) to resist greater Fair Folk magic. Wyld Shield Meditation lasts as long as the Exalt desires, although each hour that the user maintains the Charm inflicts one level of unsoakable bashing damage to her.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Lore tree, p. 192 (PDF 193).

name: Chaos-Searing Treatment
summary: For the rest of the scene, an Abyssal may channel soul-numbing death Essence into a weapon, which inflicts aggravated damage against Fair Folk and Wyld beasts as though it was made of cold iron.
requirements: Minimum Lore 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Wyld Shield Meditation.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal may channel soul-numbing death Essence into a weapon. For the rest of the scene, the weapon inflicts aggravated damage against Fair Folk and Wyld beasts as though it was made of cold iron.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Lore tree, p. 193 (PDF 194).

name: Wyld-Slaying Burst
summary: Capstone of the Daybreak Caste Lore tree; the Abyssal may unleash the full force of the Underworld against the twin enemies of life and Wyld in a spherical necrotic shockwave that erodes rock, withers trees and disintegrates Fair Folk outright.
requirements: Minimum Lore 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Radiant Blight Technique, Chaos-Searing Treatment.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal may unleash the full force of the Underworld against the twin enemies of life and Wyld. This blast erupts as a spherical shockwave from the deathknight as it sucks color and life from the landscape. The Abyssal's player rolls Intelligence + Lore + Essence. All Fair Folk spawned mutants in the area of effect suffer levels of unsoakable aggravated damage equal to the number of successes rolled. Fae slain by this Charm disintegrate outright, their glamour of illusion evaporating under the onslaught of necrotic energy. Living beings inside the blast zone suffer dice of lethal damage equal to the Abyssal's Lore rating. This burst extends to a radius of (the character's permanent Essence x 10) yards. Once this Charm has been used on an area, nothing will grow in the barren circle for months -- or even years.
cost: 30 motes, 1 Willpower, one lethal health level, 3 experience points
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Lore tree, p. 193 (PDF 194). Closes out the Daybreak Caste Lore section (7 Charms total).

name: Infallible Ailment Sense
summary: Root of the Daybreak Caste Medicine tree; by examining a patient and noting his symptoms, a character with this Charm can unerringly diagnose any physical illness with which she is familiar.
requirements: Minimum Medicine 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: By examining a patient and noting his symptoms, a character with this Charm can unerringly diagnose any physical illness with which he is familiar. Characters can also attempt to diagnose mental illness with this Charm, but this requires 30 minutes of examination and a successful Perception + Medicine roll. This Charm does not improve a character's actual medical knowledge, only her ability to recognize and correctly discern known ailments. If a character has never encountered or heard of a disease, she can only diagnose its general type and ascertain whether it is magical or not. Characters can diagnose their own physical diseases with this Charm, although they cannot objectively evaluate their own mental health.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Medicine tree ('Medicine 1'), p. 193 (PDF 194).

name: Contamination of (Form)
summary: Disease is one of the doors to the Underworld; this Charm lets an Abyssal open that door somewhat, temporarily infecting a target with a malady of Body (physical disease), Mind (derangement) or Spirit (soul-numbing despair), purchased and used separately for each form.
requirements: Minimum Medicine 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Infallible Ailment Sense.
mechanics: Disease is one of the doors to the Underworld. This Charm allows an Abyssal to open that door somewhat, temporarily infecting the target with a malady. When he purchases this Charm, a character must choose the type of illness he can inflict; characters must purchase this Charm more than once in order to spread different forms of disease. In all forms, the character must be within three yards of his intended victim to infect her. Body: the Abyssal's player chooses one of the plagues listed in the Exalted rulebook (pp. 319-321) and makes an Intelligence + Medicine roll with a difficulty equal to (the disease's Virulence - 1, minimum 1). If the roll is successful, the target must succeed on a Stamina + Resistance roll to resist infection, just as if exposed to the disease in question. The illness is noncommunicable. Mind: the Abyssal's player chooses one of the derangements listed in the Exalted rulebook (p. 281) and makes a Manipulation + Medicine roll (difficulty 3). If this roll is successful, the target succumbs to the chosen form of madness unless her player rolls a successful Willpower roll against a difficulty of the Abyssal's permanent Essence. Derangements induced by this Charm last a number of days equal to the Exalt's Manipulation rating. The actual game effects of madness are left to Storytellers to decide. Spirit: the Abyssal's player makes a Conviction + Medicine roll, resisted by his intended victim's Valor + Essence. If the Exalt wins, the target immediately falls prey to soul-numbing despair. Afflicted characters cannot regain lost Willpower and suffer a -2 penalty to all dice pools. This depression is not natural, but a form of soul rot. As such, the infection cured through mundane means can target mental illness but medicine can only be cured through supernatural remedies or willpower. Once per day, players of infected characters can roll Willpower against a difficulty of the Abyssal's permanent Essence. If successful, the character's soul recovers, and her despair lifts. Ordinary mortals infected with despair for more days than their Valor rating commit suicide. Characters cannot learn Contamination of Spirit until they have mastered the other two forms of this Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Medicine tree ('Medicine 1'/'Medicine 2'), pp. 193-195 (PDF 194-196). Modeled here as one row covering all three forms (Body/Mind/Spirit); the book presents these as one Charm purchased/learned separately per form, with Spirit gated behind learning both Body and Mind. Some phrasing in the Spirit description ('the infection cured through mundane means can target mental illness but medicine can only be cured through supernatural remedies or willpower') reads as garbled/inconsistent in the source render and should be re-checked against a cleaner scan before promotion.

name: Rampant Pestilence Method
summary: This Charm duplicates the effects of Contamination of Body with two notable exceptions: plagues created with it are more deadly and resistant to medication, and they are just plagues, spreadable to other victims by all the usual vectors.
requirements: Minimum Medicine 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Contamination of Body.
mechanics: This Charm duplicates the effects of Contamination of Body with two notable exceptions. First, plagues created with this Charm are more deadly and resistant to medication, adding +1 to the difficulty of any Endurance, Resistance or Medicine-related roll to fight off or treat them. In addition, such plagues are just plagues -- and may be spread to other victims by all the usual vectors, for the actual disease. The effects persist until the Abyssal removes the Essence committed to the Charm. After that point, the disease ceases to be contagious. Although Abyssals are immune to diseases they personally create, their fellows and allies are not, so they must be careful in the use of this Charm: Plague does not distinguish between friend and foe.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Medicine tree ('Medicine 2'), p. 194 (PDF 195). The phrase 'adding +1 to the difficulty... to fight off or treat them' is slightly garbled in the source render; interpretation given here is the most plausible reading and should be re-checked against a cleaner scan before promotion.

name: Taint Extraction Technique
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal can expunge the corruption of disease from her flesh or the flesh of another with a moment's concentration and a touch, cured of even the Great Contagion at a cost of lethal damage.
requirements: Minimum Medicine 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Contamination of Body.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can expunge the corruption of disease from his flesh or the flesh of another. All it takes is a moment of concentration and a touch, and the excised taint bursts from the patient's body as a viscous sludge. The subject is immediately cured of all infected wounds, as well as all diseases whose Difficulty to Treat is less than or equal to the Exalt's Medicine rating. This Charm can even cure the Great Contagion. Unfortunately, the violent expulsion of taint is quite traumatic -- cured patients suffer a number of levels of lethal damage equal to the Untreated Morbidity of their worst disease. This damage can only be soaked with Stamina, assuming the patient can soak lethal damage at all.
cost: 10 motes, 1 Willpower, one lethal health level
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Medicine tree ('Medicine 2'), p. 194 (PDF 195).

name: Unsurpassed Plague Kiss
summary: When the Great Contagion swept across Creation, only one in ten survived; Unsurpassed Plague Kiss unleashes this greatest of weapons through a simple touch, a weaker but noncommunicable strain that the victim must resist or die from.
requirements: Minimum Medicine 5; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Contamination of Spirit, Rampant Pestilence Method, Taint Extraction Technique.
mechanics: When the Great Contagion swept across Creation, only one in ten survived. Unsurpassed Plague Kiss unleashes this greatest of weapons with a simple touch -- albeit a weaker, noncommunicable strain. In order to avoid contracting the Contagion, the victim's player must make a reflexive Stamina + Resistance roll at difficulty 5. If this roll fails, the player must then roll to see if he character is blessed with natural immunity. If the number rolled is less than or equal to the victim's permanent Essence, she survives with only minor fever. Otherwise, the character dies painfully after a number of days equal to her Stamina. Characters that survive infection are thereafter immune to all strains of the Contagion.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Medicine tree ('Medicine 2'), p. 195 (PDF 196). Closes out the second Medicine sub-tree.

name: Flesh-Mending Discipline
summary: Root of the third Daybreak Caste Medicine sub-tree; this Charm allows an Abyssal to force the undesired taint of injury from her body, healing bashing and lethal damage with equal facility at 10 times the normal rate.
requirements: Minimum Medicine 1; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: This Charm allows an Abyssal to force the undesired taint of injury from her body, repairing broken bones and torn flesh with equal facility. While Flesh-Mending Discipline is active, the character heals bashing and lethal damage at 10 times the normal rate. This Charm does not allow the regeneration of amputated or destroyed tissue, nor may it accelerate the healing of anyone other than the Exalt. Characters may activate this Charm at any time, even while unconscious.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Medicine tree ('Medicine 3'), p. 196 (PDF 197). Also serves as a cross-Ability prerequisite for the Craft tree's Bone Graft Technique.

name: Touch of Gentle Repose
summary: Death is often a welcome release from suffering; with this Charm, an Abyssal can grant that release to a willing individual, letting the patient spend a point of Willpower to end her own life painlessly.
requirements: Minimum Medicine 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Flesh-Mending Discipline.
mechanics: Death is often a welcome release from suffering. With this Charm, an Abyssal can grant that release to a willing individual. The Exalt need only lay his hands on the subject and whisper a prayer of dedication to the Malfeans. If the patient truly wishes to die, she may spend a point of Willpower to painlessly end her own life. This decision cannot be coerced in any way, or the Charm fails. Subjects of this Charm never rise as hungry ghosts, although they are no more or less likely to linger as actual ghosts. Characters cannot use this Charm to facilitate their own suicide.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Medicine tree ('Medicine 3'), p. 196 (PDF 197).

name: Blood Mastery Technique
summary: Though Exalted seldom have to worry about bleeding to death, the Chosen can still be overcome by blood loss; once she masters this Charm, an Abyssal transcends this limitation, reflexively stanching her wounds without a roll.
requirements: Minimum Medicine 1; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Flesh-Mending Discipline.
mechanics: Though Exalted seldom have to worry about bleeding to death, the Chosen can still be overcome by blood loss. Once she masters this Charm, however, an Abyssal transcends this limitation. She can reflexively stanch her wounds without a roll, even while unconscious. Flesh contracts and pulls tight, hungrily reabsorbing any blood spilled by the original trauma. Within instants, the injury seals completely. Blood Mastery Technique does not speed healing -- it only prevents additional damage from bleeding. This Charm cannot mitigate Abyssal Caste Mark stigmata.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Medicine tree ('Medicine 3'), p. 197 (PDF 198).

name: Crimson Waterfall Attack
summary: With her knowledge of anatomy, an Abyssal with this Charm can aim her blows at an enemy's arteries; victims bleed profusely, suffering one health level of unsoakable lethal damage every minute.
requirements: Minimum Medicine 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Blood Mastery Technique.
mechanics: With her knowledge of anatomy, an Abyssal with this Charm can aim her blows at an enemy's arteries. In addition to inflicting normal damage, lethal attacks augmented with Crimson Waterfall Attack bleed profusely. All rolls to stanch the victim's bleeding have their difficulty raised by (the Abyssal's permanent Essence rating - the target's permanent Essence rating). Victims of this Charm also bleed more quickly, suffering one health level of unsoakable lethal damage every minute. Characters with Blood Mastery Technique or similar magic are immune to this Charm. Crimson Waterfall Attack is explicitly permitted to be part of a Combo with Charms of other Abilities.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Medicine tree ('Medicine 3'), p. 197 (PDF 198).

name: Winter Strikes the Forest
summary: This Charm allows an Abyssal to infuse a target with corrosive entropy; for a full day, the target heals all injuries at one-tenth of her normal rate, permitted as part of a Combo.
requirements: Minimum Medicine 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Crimson Waterfall Attack.
mechanics: This Charm allows an Abyssal to infuse a target with corrosive entropy. For a full day, the target heals all injuries at one-tenth of her normal rate. If the target has magic augmenting her healing rate, apply the reduction to her new rating. For example: Solar Exalted employing Body-Mending Meditation recover at their normal rate if cursed with this magic -- their 10x bonus canceled by the one-tenth penalty. This Charm does not inhibit magic that directly restores health levels. Once this Charm's duration expires, the target begins to heal any remaining wounds normally with no lingering ill effects. Only one application of this Charm can affect a given target at a time. This Charm is explicitly permitted to be part of a Combo with Charms of other Abilities.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Medicine tree ('Medicine 3'), p. 197 (PDF 198). Book lists both 'Duration: Instant' and 'Type: Instant' for this Charm, which is unusual (Type is normally Simple/Reflexive/Supplementary/Special); flagged for re-verification against a cleaner render in case 'Type' was misread.

name: Wound-Absorbing Method
summary: With this Charm, an Abyssal can channel Essence into his hands, drawing them closed with force of will, converting the target's most grievous wounds into lesser cuts and bruises.
requirements: Minimum Medicine 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Touch of Gentle Repose, Blood Mastery Technique.
mechanics: With this Charm, an Abyssal can channel Essence into his hands, drawing them closed with force of will. Use of this Charm leaves discolored bruises in place of deep bones, audibly sets broken bones in inconvenience, and otherwise transforms serious injury into minor inconvenience. For every 2 motes spent, the character can convert one level of lethal damage into a bashing wound level. Characters with an permanent Essence of 3 or higher can also use this Charm to heal others, although such healing is invariably quite painful. UnExalted characters treated by this Charm lose a number of Willpower points equal to the number of lethal points converted unless they are unconscious or anesthetized.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Medicine tree ('Medicine 3'), p. 197 (PDF 198).

name: Fivefold Wound-Absorbing Method
summary: Capstone of the third Daybreak Caste Medicine sub-tree; this Charm allows the Abyssal to direct a surge of eldritch power through her flesh, turning even the most grievous wounds into lesser cuts, and regenerating lost limbs and organs over time.
requirements: Minimum Medicine 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Wound-Absorbing Method.
mechanics: This Charm allows the Abyssal to direct a surge of eldritch power through her flesh, turning her most grievous wounds into lesser cuts and breaks. For every 5 motes spent, the character can instantly convert one level of aggravated damage into a lethal level. Converted wounds heal normally unless treated with further magic (such as Wound-Absorbing Method). Alternately, this Charm can be used to regenerate destroyed tissue, amputated limbs, lost eyes, etc. Eyes, fingers, teeth, mouth full of shattered teeth and other lesser maimings are each the equivalent of one health level. Lost limbs are the equivalent of two health levels. Although regeneration fueled by this Charm is continuous and requires no particular effort or rest on the part of the Abyssal, such healing is not instantaneous. Destroyed tissue takes one hour per health level to regrow.
cost: 4 motes and 1 Willpower per health level
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Medicine tree ('Medicine 3'), p. 197 (PDF 198). Closes out the Daybreak Caste Medicine section (12 Charms total across three sub-trees, counting Contamination of (Form) as one row).

name: Terrestrial Circle Sorcery
summary: Root of the Daybreak Caste Occult tree; least of all sorcery and still worlds beyond the power of most talented mortal wizards, magic of the First Circle sees much use among the deathknights.
requirements: Minimum Occult 3; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Least of all sorcery and still worlds beyond the power of most talented mortal wizards, magic of the First Circle sees much use among the deathknights. Note that invoking this Charm only enables the character to cast a single Terrestrial Circle Sorcery spell. The actual spell itself has an Essence cost, often very high, that the character must pay to actualize it. This cost is listed in the spell's description. Terrestrial Circle Sorcery can never be part of a Combo.
cost: 1 Willpower (to enable casting; spell's own Essence cost paid separately)
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Occult tree, p. 197 (PDF 198). This Charm and its three necromancy-side counterparts are the 'switches' that let a Daybreak Abyssal cast sorcery/necromancy spells; the spells themselves (Chapter Six) are a separate, larger inventory item still to be done.

name: Celestial Circle Sorcery
summary: Easily outstripping the most potent spells of the Dragon-Blooded, the magic of the Second Circle is well known in the Underworld as a weapon of the Deathlords and their Daybreak Caste servants.
requirements: Minimum Occult 4; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Terrestrial Circle Sorcery.
mechanics: Easily outstripping the most potent spells of the Dragon-Blooded, the magic of the Second Circle is well known in the Underworld as a weapon of the Deathlords and their Daybreak Caste servants. Other Abyssal Exalted must either coax or barter with these entities for power, though the sorcerer-kings of the dead are notably reticent to share their secrets. Celestial Circle Sorcery can never be part of a Combo.
cost: 2 Willpower (to enable casting; spell's own Essence cost paid separately)
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Occult tree, p. 197 (PDF 198).

name: Shadowlands Circle Necromancy
summary: Where sorcery manipulates and channels the Essence of Creation, its sister art of necromancy binds the dark energies of the Underworld; those who delve into the mystical lore of the Malfeans master this Charm to perform necromancy of the First Circle.
requirements: Minimum Occult 3; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Where sorcery manipulates and channels the Essence of Creation, its sister art of necromancy binds the dark energies of the Underworld. What it lacks in flexibility, however, it makes up for in might. Those who delve into the mystical lore of the Malfeans master this Charm to hone will and spirit to perform necromancy of the First Circle. Note that, as with sorcery, the cost of this Charm only enables the character to cast a single Shadowlands Circle spell. The actual spell itself has an Essence cost, often very high, that the character must pay to actualize it. This cost is listed in the spell's description. Shadowlands Circle Necromancy can never be part of a Combo.
cost: 1 Willpower (to enable casting; spell's own Essence cost paid separately)
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Occult tree, p. 197 (PDF 198). Enabling Charm only; the actual Shadowlands Circle spell list is Chapter Six material, still to be inventoried (see useful-crafts-underworld row's deferred-necromancy note and this round's report).

name: Labyrinth Circle Necromancy
summary: Above -- or perhaps below -- the necromancy of the First Circle, Labyrinth Circle magic is the stuff of nightmares and dreams best left to dead gods; still, for those who would master its secrets, this Charm offers grim and terrible power.
requirements: Minimum Occult 4; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Shadowlands Circle Necromancy.
mechanics: Above -- or perhaps below -- the necromancy of the First Circle, Labyrinth Circle magic is the stuff of nightmares and dreams best left to dead gods. Still, for those who would master its secrets, this Charm offers grim and terrible power. Labyrinth Circle Necromancy can never be part of a Combo.
cost: 2 Willpower (to enable casting; spell's own Essence cost paid separately)
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Occult tree, p. 198 (PDF 199). Enabling Charm only; Labyrinth Circle spell list is Chapter Six material, still to be inventoried.

name: Void Circle Necromancy
summary: In true poetic irony, the very death taint that denies the Abyssal Exalted access to Solar Circle Sorcery also grants them comparable power over the Oblivion they serve; masters of Void Circle Necromancy are thankfully rare, wielding power that would devour all Creation as well as the Underworld.
requirements: Minimum Occult 5; Minimum Essence 5; Prerequisite Charms: Labyrinth Circle Necromancy.
mechanics: In true poetic irony, the very death taint that denies the Abyssal Exalted access to Solar Circle Sorcery also grants them comparable power over the Oblivion they serve. Masters of Void Circle Necromancy are thankfully rare, but theirs is the power of unmaking, the power that would devour all Creation in its hunger -- and the Underworld as well. Few spells of this potency exist outside the personal libraries of the Deathlords; the sorcerer-kings of the Underworld zealously hoard such mighty lore as they hoard little else. Void Circle Necromancy can never be part of a Combo.
cost: 3 Willpower (to enable casting; spell's own Essence cost paid separately)
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Occult tree, p. 198 (PDF 199). Capstone of the sorcery/necromancy 'enabling Charm' quartet. Void Circle spell list is Chapter Six material, still to be inventoried.

name: Spirit Sensing Technique
summary: This Charm allows the character to perceive dematerialized spirits in her vicinity, appearing as translucent specters of their materialized form and imbued with the ability to identify other Abyssal Exalted and shadowlands boundaries.
requirements: Minimum Occult 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: This Charm allows the character to perceive dematerialized spirits in her vicinity. Such beings appear as translucent specters of their materialized form, although ghosts appear more 'solid' to the Abyssal than other types of spirits. Every 5 motes spent above the Charm's base cost allow the character to project one additional sense into the spirit realm. However, even if a character can feel the touch of a dematerialized spirit, she cannot actually touch it without employing other magic. In addition to perceiving dematerialized ghosts, objects imbued with living Essence appear shadowed or empty. Beings fused with the necrotic Essence of the Underworld leaks through Creation in wisps and places, an Abyssal can perceive these energies directly, and places imbued with living Essence appear shadowed or empty. Deathknights employing this Charm can also spot the seething ripples and whorls of Charms and sorcery, allowing them to notice magic without a roll. With a successful Intelligence + Occult roll, a character can even identify magic (although the difficulty increases by 1 if the scrutinized magic does not involve death energy).
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Occult tree ('Occult 3'), pp. 198-199 (PDF 199-200). The mechanics text repeats/garbles the description of necrotic Essence in the Underworld and living-Essence objects appearing shadowed or empty (the sentence appears twice with variation); flagged for re-verification against a cleaner render before promotion.

name: Through Dead Eyes
summary: Even in the most verdant forests, the necrotic Essence of the Underworld leaks through Creation in wisps and places an Abyssal can perceive these energies directly, spotting shadowlands boundaries and identifying other deathknights at a glance.
requirements: Minimum Occult 5; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Spirit Sensing Technique.
mechanics: Even in the most verdant forests, the necrotic Essence of the Underworld leaks through Creation in wisps and places. With this potent Charm, an Abyssal can perceive these energies directly and places infused with death glow with their own baleful radiance. In addition to perceiving dematerialized Abyssal ghosts, objects imbued with living Essence appear shadowed or empty. Beings fused with this Charm confers no ability to perceive incorporeal spirits, so characters attacking without this magic (such as Spirit Sensing Technique) suffer the usual penalty for blind fighting. This Charm has no effect on materialized spirits. Corpse-Rending Blow is explicitly permitted to be part of a Combo with Charms of other Abilities.

name: Corpse-Rending Blow
summary: Charging his hand or weapon with spectral energy, the character can make one strike against an immaterial spirit; a successful hit inflicts aggravated damage and drains Essence at the Abyssal's discretion.
requirements: Minimum Occult 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Spirit Sensing Technique.
mechanics: Charging his hand or weapon with spectral energy, the character can make one strike against an immaterial spirit. The character's player must still roll to hit the creature normally, although the deathknight may elect to attack the spirit's Essence in lieu of inflicting damage. This decision must be made before activating the Charm, before rolling the attack. If the Abyssal chooses to drain Essence, roll her Conviction + Occult using the spirit's Valor as its soak total. Each level of damage inflicted in this fashion drains 2 motes of Essence from the spirit's pool and adds it to the character's own. Drained motes that would take a character above her normal maximum are still drained but dissipate without benefit to the Exalt. If the character uses this Charm to cause actual damage, the attack is resolved normally.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Occult tree ('Occult 3'), p. 199 (PDF 200).

name: Soul-Eating Strike
summary: This Charm allows an Abyssal to infuse a single attack with the chill of the Void, inflicting aggravated damage and draining Essence from a spirit that is explicitly permitted to be part of a Combo with Charms of other Abilities.
requirements: Minimum Occult 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Corpse-Rending Blow.
mechanics: This Charm allows an Abyssal to infuse a single attack with the chill of the Void. The character's blow can strike incorporeal spirits. A successful hit inflicts aggravated damage and drains Essence as Corpse-Rending Blow (roll separately for each form of damage). Spirits slain by such attacks are irrevocably destroyed. Against materialized spirits, this Charm allows the Abyssal to drain Essence as above, but the attack does not inflict aggravated damage. Materialized spirits killed via Soul-Eating Strike eventually regenerate. This Charm is explicitly permitted to be part of a Combo with Charms of other Abilities. Spirits can sense Exalts who know this Charm and hate them for it.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Occult tree ('Occult 3'), pp. 199-200 (PDF 200-201).

name: Spirit-Draining Ward
summary: Capstone of the Daybreak Caste Occult tree; opening himself as a conduit to the Void, the Abyssal spreads his arms and a maelstrom of flickering shadows billows out to fill a radius equaling his permanent Essence in yards, battering and draining immaterial spirits within.
requirements: Minimum Occult 5; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Soul-Eating Strike.
mechanics: Opening himself as a conduit to the Void, the Abyssal spreads his arms and a maelstrom of flickering shadows billows out to fill a radius equaling his permanent Essence in yards. This effect remains centered on the character for the remainder of the scene. While visible in the material world, this unnatural storm barely raises a light breeze. However, immaterial spirits within the area of effect suffer battering cold equivalent to an arctic gale. Against such creatures, this Charm inflicts a number of levels of unsoakable aggravated damage equal to the Abyssal's permanent Essence minus the spirit's permanent Essence. This damage is not rolled. It is simply applied each turn unless the spirit has a means of soaking against damage. The character regains 2 motes of Essence for every level of damage inflicted by the ward, up to his usual maximum. Spirits killed by this Charm are sucked into the Void and permanently destroyed. Although this Charm cannot injure spirits whose Essence rating matches or exceeds the character, the ward still discomfits them (adding +1 to the difficulty of all actions inside its area of effect). Materialized spirits are immune to this Charm.
notes: Chapter Five: Charms, Daybreak Caste Occult tree ('Occult 3'), p. 200 (PDF 201). Closes out the Daybreak Caste Occult section (10 Charms total) and, with it, all five Daybreak Caste Charm trees (Craft, Investigation, Lore, Medicine, Occult).
